title: Rates of Change and Tangents to Curves
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar

definitions.title: Average Rate of Change
definitions.latex: \text{avg rate} = \frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} = \frac{f(x_2) - f(x_1)}{x_2 - x_1} = \frac{f(x_1 + h) - f(x_1)}{h}
definitions.statement: The average rate of change of a quantity y = f(x) over an interval [x1, x2] is the ratio of the change in y to the change in x.
conditions: x1 and x2 must belong to the domain of f
definitions.explanation: Geometrically, the average rate of change represents the slope of the secant line connecting points P(x1, f(x1)) and Q(x2, f(x2)) on the graph of f.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Average rate of change equals the slope of the secant line across the interval.

definitions.title: Slope of a Curve at a Point (Instantaneous Rate of Change)
definitions.statement: The slope of the curve y = f(x) at the point P(x0, f(x0)) is the limit of the secant line slopes as the increment h approaches 0, provided this limit exists.
conditions: The two-sided limit as h -> 0 must exist as a finite real number
f must be defined in an open interval containing x0
definitions.explanation: As point Q(x0+h, f(x0+h)) slides along the curve toward P(x0, f(x0)), the secant line PQ rotates into the tangent line at P.
definitions.keyTakeaway: The tangent slope is the instantaneous rate of change and the limit of difference quotients.

definitions.title: Point-Slope Equation of the Tangent Line
definitions.statement: The tangent line to the curve y = f(x) at point (x0, f(x0)) with slope m is given by y - f(x0) = m(x - x0).
conditions: Slope m = lim_{h->0} [f(x0+h) - f(x0)]/h is finite
If m is infinite and curve is continuous at x0, the tangent line is vertical: x = x0
definitions.explanation: This linear equation provides the best local straight-line approximation to the curve near x0.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Equation of tangent line requires the contact point (x0, f(x0)) and the limiting slope m.

definitions.title: Average and Instantaneous Velocity
definitions.latex: v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t} = \frac{s(t + \Delta t) - s(t)}{\Delta t}, \quad v(t) = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{s(t + \Delta t) - s(t)}{\Delta t}
definitions.statement: For an object whose position along a coordinate line is s(t), average velocity is displacement over elapsed time, and instantaneous velocity is the time limit of average velocity.
conditions: Position function s(t) is defined over the observation interval
definitions.explanation: Instantaneous velocity indicates both the speed (magnitude) and direction of motion at an exact instant.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Instantaneous velocity is the derivative of the position function with respect to time.
